sections.title: Conditions
sections.subtitle: Common effects that change what a creature can do.
items: • Creature can’t see and automatically fails any ability check that requires sight.
• Disadv. on attacks, adv. on attacks vs creature.
• When a creature has ½ its HP remaining.
• Can’t attack or target the charmer with damaging abilities or magical effects.
• Charmer has adv. on social checks vs creature.
• Disadv. on ability checks and attacks while source of fear is in line of sight.
• Can’t willingly move closer to source of fear.
• Disadv. on all attacks and ability checks.
• Cumulative, +1 level every time it is received.
• Creature dies if Exhaustion Level is 6.
• −2 to D20 Tests and −5 ft. to Speed per level.
• Creature can’t take any action, bonus action or reaction, and cannot speak.
• Finishing a Long Rest reduces Exhaustion by 1 level.
• Creature’s Speed is 0 and cannot increase.
• Disadv. on attacks vs targets except grappler.
• Grappler can drag or carry target, but every foot costs 1 additional foot unless the target is Tiny or 2 sizes smaller.
• Condition ends if grappler is Incapacitated, distance exceeds grapple range, or target escapes.
• Creature’s Speed is 0 and cannot increase.
• Disadv. on attacks, adv. on attacks vs creature.
• Always fails STR and DEX saving throws.
• Creature is unaffected by effects that require its target to be seen unless the effect’s creator can somehow see it.
• Adv. on attacks, disadv. on attacks vs creature. Does not apply to other creatures that can somehow see it.
• Creature’s Speed is 0 and cannot increase.
• Always fails STR and DEX saving throws.
• Adv. on attacks vs creature. Attacks are always critical hits if attacker is within 5 ft. of creature.
• Creature is transformed, along with any non-magical objects worn or carried, into a solid inanimate substance (stone). Weight increases by ×10, and the creature ceases aging.
• Creature can’t hear, automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.
• Creature can only crawl unless it spends ½ its Speed to stand up, ending the condition.
• Can’t stand up if Speed is 0.
• Disadv. on attacks, adv. on attacks vs creature if attacker is within 5 ft.; otherwise disadv. on attacks vs creature instead.
• May choose to drop prone on player turn without using actions or movement, unless Speed is 0.
• Creature is Incapacitated, drops Prone, and drops whatever it is holding. The creature remains Prone when this condition ends.

• Adv. on attacks vs creature. Attacks are always critical hits if attacker is within 5 ft. of creature.

columnItems: [👁️‍🗨️] Blinded
• Creature can’t see and automatically fails any ability check that requires sight.
• Disadv. on attacks, adv. on attacks vs creature.
[🩸] Bloodied
• When a creature has ½ its HP remaining.
[♡] Charmed
• Can’t attack or target the charmer with damaging abilities or magical effects.
• Charmer has adv. on social checks vs creature.
[ϟ] Frightened
• Disadv. on ability checks and attacks while source of fear is in line of sight.
• Can’t willingly move closer to source of fear.
[☠] Poisoned
• Disadv. on all attacks and ability checks.
[☠] Exhaustion
• Cumulative, +1 level every time it is received.
• Creature dies if Exhaustion Level is 6.
• −2 to D20 Tests and −5 ft. to Speed per level.
[✦] Incapacitated
• Creature can’t take any action, bonus action or reaction, and cannot speak.
• Creature’s Concentration is broken.
• Surprised: Disadv. on initiative rolls.
• Finishing a Long Rest reduces Exhaustion by 1 level.
[↗] Grappled
• Creature’s Speed is 0 and cannot increase.
• Disadv. on attacks vs targets except grappler.
• Grappler can drag or carry target, but every foot costs 1 additional foot unless the target is Tiny or 2 sizes smaller.
• Condition ends if grappler is Incapacitated, distance exceeds grapple range, or target escapes.
[⛓] Restrained
• Creature’s Speed is 0 and cannot increase.
• Disadv. on attacks, adv. on attacks vs creature.
• Disadv. on DEX saving throws.
[✹] Stunned
• Creature is Incapacitated.
• Always fails STR and DEX saving throws.
• Adv. on attacks vs creature.
[👻] Invisible
• Surprise: Adv. on initiative rolls.
• Creature is unaffected by effects that require its target to be seen unless the effect’s creator can somehow see it.
• Adv. on attacks, disadv. on attacks vs creature. Does not apply to other creatures that can somehow see it.
[⛓] Paralyzed
• Creature is Incapacitated.
• Creature’s Speed is 0 and cannot increase.
• Always fails STR and DEX saving throws.
• Adv. on attacks vs creature. Attacks are always critical hits if attacker is within 5 ft. of creature.
[🪨] Petrified
• Creature is transformed, along with any non-magical objects worn or carried, into a solid inanimate substance (stone). Weight increases by ×10, and the creature ceases aging.
[◌] Deafened
• Creature can’t hear, automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.
[⬇] Prone
• Creature can only crawl unless it spends ½ its Speed to stand up, ending the condition.
• Can’t stand up if Speed is 0.
• Disadv. on attacks, adv. on attacks vs creature if attacker is within 5 ft.; otherwise disadv. on attacks vs creature instead.
• May choose to drop prone on player turn without using actions or movement, unless Speed is 0.
[😵] Unconscious
• Creature is Incapacitated, drops Prone, and drops whatever it is holding. The creature remains Prone when this condition ends.
• Creature’s Speed is 0 and cannot increase.
• Adv. on attacks vs creature. Attacks are always critical hits if attacker is within 5 ft. of creature.
• Always fails STR and DEX saving throws.
• Creature is unaware of its surroundings.
• If creature has 0 HP and is stabilised, regains 1 HP after 1d4 hours.

sections.title: Actions in combat
sections.subtitle: General actions and common physical options on your turn.
items: • Make one melee or ranged attack, or use an Unarmed Strike.
• Gain extra movement for the current turn.
• Movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks for the rest of the turn.
• Attacks against you have disadvantage; you have advantage on Dexterity saves.
• Help an ability check or attack roll, or administer first aid.
• Make a Dexterity (Stealth) check to become hidden.
• Use Deception, Intimidation, Performance, Persuasion, or Animal Handling to alter an attitude.
• Cast a spell, use a magic item, or use a magical feature.
• Prepare to take an action in response to a trigger you define.
• Make an Insight, Medicine, Perception, or Survival check to find or notice something.
• Make an Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, or Religion check to recall information.
• Use a nonmagical object when it requires an action.
• Use your movement for a Long Jump or High Jump; see Jump distance.
• Attack option: on a hit, the target makes a Strength or Dexterity save or becomes Grappled.
• Attack option: on a hit, the target makes a Strength or Dexterity save or is pushed 5 ft. or knocked Prone.
• Throw an object as an improvised attack, or use it with Utilize when the object requires an action.

sections.title: Damage calculation
sections.subtitle: Fast reminder for attack and damage rolls.
items: • d20 + ability modifier + proficiency bonus (if proficient) + other bonuses.
• Weapon or spell damage die + relevant ability modifier + other bonuses.
• Roll all of the attack’s damage dice twice, then add modifiers once.

sections.title: Concentration
sections.subtitle: Keeping a spell active when you take damage.
items: Whenever you take damage while concentrating on a spell, make a Constitution saving throw to maintain concentration. DC equals 10 or half the damage taken, whichever number is higher.

sections.title: Movement rules
sections.subtitle: Special movement and difficult terrain.
items: Crawling without a crawl speed costs 1 extra foot per foot.
Climbing without a climb speed costs 1 extra foot per foot.
Swimming without a swim speed costs 1 extra foot per foot.
Difficult terrain costs 1 extra foot per foot moved.

sections.title: Suffocation
sections.subtitle: Breath-holding and running out of air.
items: A creature can hold its breath for 1 + Constitution modifier minutes (minimum 30 seconds). If it runs out of breath, it can survive for a number of rounds equal to its Constitution modifier before dropping to 0 hit points.

sections.title: Stealth / sneak
sections.subtitle: Use when a creature hides or moves unseen.
items: • Make a Dexterity (Stealth) check while heavily obscured, behind cover, or out of line of sight.
• The check total becomes the DC for a creature to find you with Wisdom (Perception).
• You are revealed after making a sound louder than a whisper, attacking, or casting a spell with a verbal component.
• You have advantage on attacks and enemies have disadvantage attacking you, unless they can somehow see you.

sections.title: Jump distance
sections.subtitle: Movement calculations at a glance.
items: • If you move at least 10 ft. immediately before the jump, cover a number of feet up to your Strength score.
• If you do not move 10 ft. first, jump only half that distance.
• If you move at least 10 ft. immediately before the jump, leap a number of feet equal to 3 + your Strength modifier.
• If you do not move 10 ft. first, jump only half that distance.
• Add your reach to the jump height if you can make an arm-assisted jump.
• Every foot of movement costs 1 extra foot when moving through difficult terrain.

sections.title: Random things
sections.subtitle: Small details to add life to a scene.
items: • A cracked sign, a lost button, a cold coin, or a letter with no name.
• Something burnt, overly sweet, spiced, sour, or unexpectedly fresh.
• A missing glove, bright sash, muddy hem, or unusual uniform.
• A custom, warning, rumour, payment, or small superstition.

sections.title: DM calculation reminders
sections.subtitle: Short formulas for common moments.
items: • 10 + all modifiers that normally apply to the check.
• Roll two d20s; use the higher roll with advantage or lower roll with disadvantage.
• 1d6 bludgeoning damage per 10 feet fallen, maximum 20d6.
• d20: 10+ is a success, 9 or lower is a failure; a natural 20 restores 1 HP.

sections.title: Remember the villain
sections.subtitle: Questions that make an antagonist feel real.
items: • What does this villain want to achieve?
• Why do they refuse the easier path?
• How have they changed over time?
• What experience made them choose this path?
• What would make them abandon their goal?
• What do they fear losing more than they want to win?
